notes.title: 2 in 1 update with something cool for everyone
notes.notes:
Hey Gemini II Squad!

We’ve made some updates to the game, just in time for the upcoming Summer Sale discounts.

Firstly, we added the Free-Roaming Mode to the game. If you have already completed the campaign, now you can start a new game, with all doors, elevators and key items unlocked. Collecting leftover Specimens and exploring will now be much more convenient and you also get a quicker way to unlock the other ending.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/9761e37617ea9656e346722be3457726d943673c.png

Now, let’s move on to the second item on the agenda…

The Warlock from Project Warlock retro shooter has joined the Gemini II Squad as a playable character in the previous patch and was supposed to be available only for a limited time. But we heard you. *drumroll* The Warlock is here to stay and becomes a full-fledged Gemini II Squad member! He’s now available as a free DLC, so be sure to add it to your Library (sorry for the inconvenience!).

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2060270/Warlock_character_for_BIOTA/

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/9bc2c24b0cfe252fdbc3f106e5ee9c7eccf8be67.png

We’re constantly going through your feedback and encourage you to leave a Steam review if you like the game because they help us get in front of more players.

Thanks for checking in, and see you next time!

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26858/Project_Warlock_2_x_BIOTA_Bundle/

notes.title: B.I.O.T.A. patch 1.015 is now available
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Thank you for your ongoing support! We encourage you to keep playing B.I.O.T.A. and let us know what you think about it, whether it’s in the forums, Steam reviews, or on our Discord server.

We’re very grateful for the constant feedback and bug reports. We’re working on bug fixes and making the game even better.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/4df40c8c0566f553cc7256432d321a120ac1cf96.png

Here’s the list of major changes introduced in the 1.015 version:

 New messages for can’t-save triggers. Now you will know exactly what’s stopping you from saving the game, whether there are enemies nearby, bullets flying around, or other threats. 
 The can’t-save zones have been perfected. Cases have been tweaked zone-by-zone. Now you should be able to save unless you are close to a trap.
 Markers for key cards and viridium containers have been added to the map (dot-shaped markers) This change should account for better navigation throughout the game.
 Windowed mode was added in the settings menu. Windowed mode was available through a hidden command (Ctrl+1). But now it’s visible in the settings for everyone who prefers windowed mode over fullscreen!
 Fixed a bug that prevents collecting  2 specimens in the sub-area. You haven’t been the only ones squashing (alien) bugs this week.
 Added an autosave point after switching off the reactor. For extra safety.


We’re constantly going through the feedback and we encourage you to share your impressions and recommend us to your friends. We’re also grateful for every Steam review as they help us get in front of more players and keep us going!

We’ve also launched a new special offer with a 10% extra discount if you grab Project Warlock and B.I.O.T.A. or already own one of them and decide to buy another.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/25009/

notes.title: B.I.O.T.A. Dev Update #4: The last stretch...
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

We’re coming to you with another Dev Update. This one will be quick and short, but we still wanted to check-in, as it has become our monthly tradition.

If you would like to check out how the development of B.I.O.T.A. looks, make sure to check out our Live Dev episodes, in which Ivan took everyone behind the scenes of our metroidvania platformer.

[previewyoutube=Q4OdNKYlDHo;full][/previewyoutube]

While the first episode focused on some behind the scenes stuff inside the editor, the second one revolved around live playthrough and debugging. 

[previewyoutube=1bYhaP6AMyM;full][/previewyoutube]

The last few weeks of B.I.O.T.A.’s development revolved around localization, squashing bugs, and tuning stuff like life-damage ratio, enemy placement, and all other variables.

We’ve also created 4 color palettes that are color-blind friendly! You can check them out here 

To tease you a bit more, check out this gif, we’ve prepared. We can’t wait for you to jump into this mech and destroy some alien spawns.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/61750b47b41275f6acb56af2824478692f78f2fd.gif

We’re getting closer and closer to finishing B.I.O.T.A., so stay on the lookout for some special announcements in the near future 👀.

As always, please follow and wishlist B.I.O.T.A., and spread the word. Make sure to join our official Discord to share your feedback and thoughts about our game!


See you next time!

notes.title: B.I.O.T.A. Dev Update #3 - The Pegasus finally takes it to the skies
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

It’s a brand new year, so it’s time for some fresh news about B.I.O.T.A.’s development.

First of all, it took some time, but we’ve finished the Dogfight segment of B.I.O.T.A. In this part of the game, you’ll pilot the Pegasus and face the Centurion in close-range combat. It’s something entirely different from the rest of the game, and we can’t wait for you to try it!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/6db9d0a2cb3de35198e7a41944983749e12a29e3.gif

Another segment we’ve finished recently is the Space Hornet Swarm. This time you’ll need to take down a swarm of giant mutant space hornets using a moving Space Cannon. Larger enemies require larger and heavier-hitting guns.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/79df2a7a500705eda8ee7f5d0db5d36ecb3074d4.gif

We’ve also added new special weapons for two agents. Nebula for Unit-34 and Storm Machine for Kirill. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/e042bc6cac59d038e0f8efd4936453343ed53deb.gif

As you can see, Nebula sends a cluster of energy charges around the agent, the walls don’t stop the projectiles, so it will be a great tool to clear whole rooms.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/7eddd4e466ad1bcbc181f30366a729644b9ff2a5.gif

While we’re talking about clearing whole rooms, take a look at the Storm Machine for Kirill. It brings thunder and destructive rain, damaging everything around.

Apart from new things, we’ve spent time polishing the game and tweaking details like item prices in the stores.

Let us know what you think about the game and we hope to see you on our official Discord.

See you next time!

notes.title: B.I.O.T.A. Dev Update #2 - Meet Alex, a new playable character
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

We’d like to be faster than Santa and deliver you some fresh news about B.I.O.T.A.’s development before the Holidays!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/4c266374c26ce6791c9ca7ea32721cad53d91e0e.gif

First up, the new character - Alex a.k.a. the Hitman. Her past remains a mystery, but it is said that she has made a fortune working for an organization of professional killers. She specializes in stealth and silent weapons. Her B-ray Gun makes the enemies look like sitting ducks,, and her special Cluster Neutron Bomb ability annihilates every enemy in the blast zone. See for yourselves!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/01896ef6919b70d1c822a7ef0715d74d90fdfa07.gif

We’ve also finished the SHMUP section of the game which adds another layer to the gameplay experience in B.I.O.T.A. In this section, you’ll control a shuttle, collect weapon upgrades, and plow through a field of enemies. We hope it’ll bring back your fond memories of classic Shoot’em Ups.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/6f8512bae3ad912bb813e5072106faecb5c5b135.gif

As for new settings, we’ve added the option to choose between Lo-Fi and Hi-Fi Color Rendering. It’s very likely that most players will be able to choose the Hi-Fi option and play without any issues, while the Lo-Fi setting is optimized for integrated graphic cards. This will allow lower-end PCs to run the game without any issues.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/a48d3b738101c77828db7efaae768a864f6e2bce.gif

One last minor update is the Cutscene Frame. We thought it was a bit dull and empty, so we’ve decided to change it completely.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/1fb40aa3dbadfa8c6bb0ba25867b6ca6035d3939.png

As B.I.O.T.A. nears completion, we’re working out the last stages of the game and adding finishing touches across the board. We’ll have more info to share in January. Follow B.I.O.T.A. here on Steam, so you don’t miss it!

That’s all for this Dev Update. Let us know what you think about the game and we hope to see you on our official Discord.

See you next time!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1640320/BIOTA/

notes.title: B.I.O.T.A. Dev Update #1 - Latest updates after the demo
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

After the last demo update, we wanted to let you know about how things are going with B.I.O.T.A.’s development. We also hope updates like this will become more frequent! 

Let's dive into new features coming to B.I.O.T.A.

First off, the Training Cabin inside the HQ (previously a tutorial) has now become a new mini-game that will allow you to earn credits while mastering the game mechanics. The prize will be proportional to the time needed to finish the obstacle course. Satisfaction from beating your own high scores will be added fun here.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/588c6147166e313a4df798981962debd3cc3b3a9.gif

Another aspect that we’ve worked on is gem farming. We don’t want you to spend hours on a tedious grind for gems. Everyone needs credits for upgrades, so we want to speed up the process of earning them. In order to accomplish that, we’re introducing two types of gems: Large Gem worth 5 credits and Small Gem worth 2 credits. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/20ceac88681c0c369a2d13305f4e8222867df48a.gif

Many of you asked for more agency in terms of settings, especially audio settings, so we’ve expanded the audio options menu. Players will be able to turn off the rumble controller and adjust the volume of SFX and music separately. Thank you all for feedback on this, and please keep letting us know about your ideas and suggestions after playing the demo.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/b55b8bb43fa75ddc9843014e25926c14750e7562.png

We’re also thinking of new ways you could play the game and have fun, as we feel that the base mode has a lot of potential to branch out.

Firstly we plan to introduce the Arcade Time Attack mode, similar to the tutorial mini-game, but much bigger. You’ll have to complete a simulated path that runs through all 10 Frontier Horizon areas in the shortest time possible. Each death would additionally lower your final time. We can’t wait for you to try it and to hear your suggestions for other alternative modes in B.I.O.T.A.!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/15e96a5b8e8a10b1f302e6144a9b449db090f66c.gif

We’re also testing the Permadeath Mode in which every character who dies during the story is permanently eliminated. It’s still at an early stage of development, so stay tuned for more details.

To end this update on a slimy note, we’d like to mention a new type of obstacle...

B.I.O.T.A.'s mutants produce looooots of slime. In zone 6, you’ll have to run through layers of muck covering the floor and platforms. Step carefully, so you don’t slip into the pools of acid. You could say that now even the floor is trying to kill you. Welp, just B.I.O.T.A. things!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40648069/17786cd46f95d73b83c55ae508f5bd9f116a347f.gif

That’s all for this Dev Update. Let us know what you think about new features on the Steam forum, or our Retrovibe Discord.

Remember to follow B.I.O.T.A. here on Steam, wishlist the game, and tell your friends.

See you next time!
